name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 19 points with an entrenched incumbent running
Thompson's roughly 15-to-1 fundraising edge ($2.1M raised vs. $139K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
Democratic-friendly national environment is the only factor cutting against Thompson
model.rationale: Thompson combines a nineteen-point district lean, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising advantage in a race with no polls, no expert ratings, and essentially no outside spending signaling competitiveness. Only a historic Democratic wave, far beyond the current environment, could put this seat in play.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the race inside ten points or a sudden influx of outside spending against Thompson would warrant revisiting the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-15 is a heavily Republican district, and incumbent Glenn Thompson enters the general election with every structural advantage. No public polls or expert ratings track this race, but the district's Republican lean of roughly nineteen points and Thompson's incumbency set a very high bar for Democrat Ray Bilger. Thompson has raised about $2.1 million to Bilger's $140,000, a roughly fifteen-to-one financial edge, and holds more than $700,000 on hand for the fall. Prediction markets give Thompson about a 96 percent chance of winning.

A national environment favorable to Democrats is the main factor working in Bilger's favor, but it would need to be historic to overcome a district that leans so heavily Republican. Neither side is spending meaningful outside money here, a sign both view the contest as out of play. The expected margin sits deep in Republican territory with little evidence pointing to a competitive race.
